Authors hedge the cause of the tubular damage ("possibly related to TDF", enhanced by a preexisting renal impairment secondary to chemotherapy) and in the discussion say chemotherapy "could have played an important role". Table 1 lists the risk factor as Ifosfamide, Cisplatin.

The abstract calls the infection severe acute HBV hepatitis, while the case text reports moderate elevation in aminotransferases and INR (1.40) and the discussion says only laboratory alterations without clinical findings.
The infection source is hypothesized as "his surgical or oncological course" and the discussion says the authors do not know how the child became infected.
Several units are printed in nonstandard form (AST 280 UI/ml and ALT 620 UI/ml vs ALT 456 U/L; HBV-DNA with dot-separated digits; "4log(10)" decrease).

Figure 1 data labels and axis values are pixel content (visual.json only). The printed serum phosphate label at month 5 agrees with the phosphatemia 1.9 mg/dl that the case text states independently after 5 months of TDF treatment; the text fact stays scored because it is not taken from the image, and the other printed labels are not used as facts.
